ai.description: This snake reaches 20–30 cm. It is dark brown above with a yellow-spotted belly and a small, pointed head. The tail ends in a flat, bicarinate shield.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis arcticeps* is best distinguished by its uniquely truncated, shield-like tail ending in a distinct, bicarinate (two-ridged) terminal scale.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis arcticeps* inhabits the moist, leaf-littered floors of evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the southern Western Ghats at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: *Uropeltis arcticeps* is a nocturnal burrower that spends most of its life underground, emerging to the surface primarily during or after heavy monsoon rains.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis arcticeps* is viviparous, giving birth to live young. While specific clutch sizes and breeding seasons remain poorly documented, it follows typical uropeltid traits.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis arcticeps* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, typically inhabiting mid-to-high elevation forests.
